verdict.rationale: Snoozing is clearly documented: a snoozed conversation is hidden until a chosen time and then returns to the Inbox, and you can trigger it by swipe or the ⌘K command bar. A community user also confirms the snooze feature exists, though they criticize its inconsistent selector. The 'resurface if nobody replies' half has no per-thread follow-up reminder in evidence. The closest match is multi-step rules that wait, check conditions and act on unanswered conversations, which is an automation-level approximation rather than a user-set reminder. Missing for 10: a documented per-conversation follow-up reminder that resurfaces the thread only if no reply arrives, and an option to cancel the snooze on reply.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can snooze conversations and set follow-up reminders that resurface a thread if nobody replies

citations.quote: Snoozing temporarily hides a conversation until a specific time, then brings it back to your Inbox.
You can also snooze by swiping a conversation (configurable in Settings > Preferences > Swipes), or by opening the command bar with ⌘/Ctrl + K and typing "snooze".
Rules can now run in steps over time. Each step waits, checks its own conditions, then acts on the same conversation.
Escalate unanswered support emails: label at 24 hrs, notify the lead at 48, reassign at 72.
